## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems. The proposal includes a planned small-scale test of a 'decline feedback' channel, asking beneficiaries who decline automated offers to optionally share their reasons, to improve targeting and communication. Furthermore, the proposal includes a planned small, targeted test of a 'pre-emptive information' channel. This test would send a brief, plain-language summary of data usage and privacy safeguards alongside the initial offer message, aiming to build trust and increase opt-in rates. Additionally, the proposal includes a planned, small-scale test of a 'reverse notification' feature. This would allow users to proactively and securely flag a life event (e.g., job loss) within the government app to trigger the automated eligibility check, providing a bridge for events not automatically captured by registration systems. This would proactively notify users who have accepted automated support for one life event (e.g., job loss) if they become eligible for a subsequent, related support (e.g., a retraining allowance) after a predefined period, aiming to ensure seamless support through evolving circumstances.

A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The proposal also includes a planned small-scale test of a 'trusted intermediary' consent model. In this test, a citizen could authorize a pre-vetted community organization (e.g., a local family center) to receive and help them understand the automated offer on their behalf, specifically for non-digital users.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems. The proposal includes a planned small-scale test of a 'decline feedback' channel, asking beneficiaries who decline automated offers to optionally share their reasons, to improve targeting and communication. Furthermore, the proposal includes a planned small, targeted test of a 'pre-emptive information' channel. This test would send a brief, plain-language summary of data usage and privacy safeguards alongside the initial offer message, aiming to build trust and increase opt-in rates. Additionally, the proposal includes a planned, small-scale test of a 'reverse notification' feature. This would allow users to proactively and securely flag a life event (e.g., job loss) within the government app to trigger the automated eligibility check, providing a bridge for events not automatically captured by registration systems. The proposal also includes a planned small-scale test of a 'trusted intermediary' consent model. In this test, a citizen could authorize a pre-vetted community organization (e.g., a local family center) to receive and help them understand the automated offer on their behalf, specifically for non-digital users. Furthermore, the proposal includes a planned, small test of a 'peer ambassador' program. In this test, a select group of early users who had positive experiences with the automated service would be given a platform to share their stories (in video or text format) via official channels, to build social proof and trust.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A proposed enhancement to this model is a hypothetical partnership with a select number of trusted, non-governmental community organizations to act as 'digital navigators' for the phone line and service centers. These navigators would specifically assist non-digital users in understanding and responding to the automated offers, thereby testing an enhanced inclusion model. The proposed test of the 'trusted intermediary' consent model would be integrated into this navigator partnership, allowing authorized organizations to act as formal intermediaries for consenting users. The proposed 'peer ambassador' test content would be disseminated through these same official channels. ## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Residents from all backgrounds, selected randomly to reflect the population, and policy teams in government entities working on new regulations or services.

The initiative proposes that for selected policies, a group of about 25 residents would meet in four facilitated sessions, receive balanced information, hear from experts, and produce written recommendations. Run by a small facilitation unit, with sessions held in community centers and online.

Funded from a central innovation budget; participants would receive a small allowance for their time.

Random selection brings in voices that consultations usually miss.

Proposed indicators include the share of recommendations adopted, participant trust in government before and after, and diversity of participants.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed early wellbeing check for students that would use a short, private monthly questionnaire to help school counsellors spot students who may be struggling, before problems become serious.

## Problem

Mental health difficulties among young people often go unnoticed until they affect attendance, grades, or safety. School counsellors have many students and few ways to know who needs help first.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Students aged 12 to 18 in public schools, their parents, and school counsellors.

The initiative proposes a five-minute monthly questionnaire on a school device, based on validated wellbeing questions. Delivered through schools, with training for counsellors and a clear referral path to health services for serious cases.

The plan is to fund it from the education wellbeing budget.

It turns wellbeing support from reactive to early and gives counsellors a way to prioritise.

Proposed indicators include the number of students supported early, counsellor response times, and student-reported wellbeing over the school year.

Privacy concerns from parents are a major risk; the initiative plans parental consent, strict data access rules, and no link to grades or discipline records.

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it. This administrative burden is compounded by the fragmentation of support programs across different agencies, which creates a complex landscape that citizens must navigate on their own, often while experiencing significant stress or financial pressure.

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.
--- END PROJECT ---

Incomplete rehabilitation leads to slower recovery and more hospital readmissions. ## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases Patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or stroke, especially elderly patients and people living far from clinics, and the family members who support them. ## Solution / Service Overview The initiative proposes linking existing health and administrative records, with the patient's consent, so that eligibility for a digital rehabilitation pathway could be checked in the background when a qualifying health event (like hospital discharge) is registered. # One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies, such as hidden water leaks, by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A typical use case is a household on a low income where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as options for subsidized repair, bill relief, or financial aid.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the rules linking utility data alerts and life-event data to support eligibility. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. Each participating entity (utilities, hospital departments, and government agencies) would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water). Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and the streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government services wait for people to apply, especially after a crisis has already caused financial harm. This proposal reverses the direction: by fusing operational data (like meter readings) with social support systems, the government would come to the citizen at the moment a hidden emergency is detected and proactively offer a pre-configured bundle of support. This combined approach of automatic, data-triggered outreach and bundled, home-based therapy is rare in public service delivery.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves uptake, health outcomes, and reduces financial stress compared to the current system where citizens must seek out each service separately after discovering a crisis.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies, such as hidden water leaks, by analyzing smart meter data and automatically offers eligible citizens experiencing major life events a streamlined bundle of support, including financial relief and guided home-based therapies.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected via smart meter data shortly after a family member is discharged from the hospital following a stroke. The residents would receive an alert and, because their vulnerable status triggered by the life event is known to social services, be automatically presented with a bundled package of support options.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through a lightweight government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for those not comfortable with digital tools. A small central team would maintain the rules linking utility data alerts and life-event registrations to support eligibility. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology. Each participating data entity (e.g., utilities, hospitals, social agencies) would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support.

Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. # One-Sentence Summary

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected via smart meter data shortly after a family member is discharged from the hospital following a stroke. The residents would receive an alert and, because their vulnerable status triggered by the life event is known to social services, be automatically presented with a bundled package of support options.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options. **A proposed addition is to incorporate a digital tool for monitoring and managing medication adherence into the rehabilitation package. # One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively identifies individuals experiencing major life events, such as becoming an informal caregiver, and automatically offers them a streamlined bundle of support, including financial relief and guided home-based therapies, triggered by the detection of a household utility emergency.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs and a potential impetus for entrepreneurship: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after major medical events. A specific focus is proposed for **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, who may seek to formalize their skills into a home-based care or wellness business. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected via smart meter data shortly after a family member assumes a new caregiving role. The residents would receive an alert and, because their vulnerable status triggered by the life event is known to social services, be automatically presented with a bundled package of support options.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through one online form that asks each question once and routes the answers to every relevant entity in parallel. A guided checklist would tell the applicant exactly which supports they are eligible for. A single case manager would be proposed for any application that gets stuck. Entities would connect through a shared data exchange. Support would also be available through a helpdesk and service centers for those not comfortable with digital tools. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. This proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event and utility data (with consent), the system would proactively identify the at-risk household and come to them at the moment of imminent danger or acute need with a pre-configured bundle of specific, actionable protections and supports, which is rare in public service delivery.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves uptake and outcomes and reduces financial stress compared to the current system where citizens must discover crises and seek out each service separately.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. Wrong eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases. To avoid annoyance, detection thresholds for utility alerts would be set conservatively in a proposed first phase. Resistance from entities to sharing data or changing processes would be mitigated by starting with a pilot involving a few willing entities and a limited set of life events.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, as these individuals often become the de facto patient support system while also facing new logistical and emotional burdens. The initiative also proposes to explicitly include **households in temporary or insecure housing**, such as those in social housing, emergency accommodation, or on short-term tenancies, as these residents are particularly vulnerable to the financial shock of a utility emergency and may lack the agency or resources to arrange repairs. **A proposed expansion of the target beneficiaries is to include **recent immigrants and refugees during their first two years of residency**. This group often faces significant challenges navigating unfamiliar utility systems, housing norms, and social support networks, and may be especially vulnerable to the combined shock of a utility emergency and a major life event in a new environment.** A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke and is in a temporary housing arrangement, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support, which could also include resources for the informal caregiver and specific protections against tenancy disruption due to the emergency.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options. A proposed addition to the solution is the integration of a **digital assistant** within the support package. This would be a simple, voice- and text-enabled interface accessible via the provided app or a dedicated low-cost device for those without a smartphone. It would proactively guide the household through the bundled support steps (e.g., “Your repair technician is scheduled for tomorrow at 10 AM. Would you like me to remind you?”), answer basic questions about the services offered, and help schedule or reschedule therapy sessions, all without requiring navigation of separate agency websites or phone trees.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package, triggered by the fusion of utility data alerts and life-event data, would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools. Each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support. A proposed addition to the funding model is a targeted partnership with regulated utility companies, where a portion of the demonstrable savings from reduced water loss and avoided billing disputes is directly reinvested by the utilities into the program's operational costs. This would create a sustainable, performance-based funding stream tied directly to the value the initiative creates for the utility sector.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. It would not just alert a household to a leak and offer a subsidy for repairs, but would, in the same proactive step, integrate support from health, social services, and housing agencies tailored to a detected major life event, creating a unified safety net triggered by a single data point.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. # One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, as these individuals often become the de facto patient support system while also facing new logistical and emotional burdens. The initiative also proposes to explicitly include **households in temporary or insecure housing**, such as those in social housing, emergency accommodation, or on short-term tenancies, as these residents are particularly vulnerable to the financial shock of a utility emergency and may lack the agency or resources to arrange repairs. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke and is in a temporary housing arrangement, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support, which could also include resources for the informal caregiver and specific protections against tenancy disruption due to the emergency.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package, triggered by the fusion of utility data alerts and life-event data, would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools. Each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. ## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. ## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. ## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. Each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data. **The initiative proposes to pilot the delivery of the bundled support package through trusted, place-based intermediaries such as community health centers, public libraries, and social housing resident associations. These intermediaries would act as local hubs where citizens could receive in-person assistance to understand and activate their support package, access the loaned devices, and get help navigating the integrated services, thereby ensuring the digital-first coordination model does not exclude those with low digital literacy or trust. A proposed key enhancement is the integration of a peer-support element within these local hubs, where trained volunteers who have previously navigated similar life events and utility crises would be available to offer guidance and mentorship to new recipients of the bundled support package, fostering community resilience and trust in the system.**

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. The proposed model is also novel in its *institutional logic*: it shifts the service paradigm from a reactive, eligibility-based claim system to a proactive, vulnerability-based offer system, fundamentally redefining the government's role from a passive provider of entitlements to an active steward of wellbeing.
